name: telkomsel-product-mcp

tools.name: telkomsel_get_capabilities
tools.description:
Describe what this MCP route can answer, so a retrieval router can plan against it instead of guessing.

Read this once, then call the real tools directly. It is free: the manifest is static and makes no upstream request.

Use it to decide:
  - whether this route is the right one for a question (see routingHints)
  - which tool fits a question shape (see tools[].answers)
  - which fields exist, their types and units, and which to request (see entities)
  - which fields must be read from live data rather than an indexed copy (see trust.authoritativeFields)
  - the Indonesian to English vocabulary of the catalogue (see concepts)
  - what belongs in a retrieval index and what must never go in one (see corpus)

Deliberately does not repeat tool names, descriptions or JSON schemas: MCP already publishes those through tools/list. This carries only the semantic layer the protocol has no field for.

Args:
  - response_format (string, optional): "markdown" (default) or "json". Use "json" when a router is consuming it.

Returns (markdown): a readable summary. (json): { route, fieldSelection, entities, subEntities, trust, concepts, routingHints, tools, corpus }

response_format.description: "markdown" for a readable table, "json" for machine-readable output.

tools.name: telkomsel_resolve_intent
tools.description:
Turn what a customer says into the query the catalogue actually answers.

A customer types "paket buat nonton". The Telkomsel catalogue never uses the words "nonton buat", and the brands it does name — Prime Video, WeTV, Vision+ — are not words a customer would guess. This tool is the bridge, and it exists because the mapping cannot be derived: a retrieval router knows language, not which apps an Indonesian telco bundles this month.

Every term it returns was validated against the live catalogue and is re-counted on each call, so a term that has disappeared reports 0 instead of silently returning nothing. Where the catalogue has no answer at all — it contains no package described as "unlimited", and never uses the words "murah" or "diskon" — that is reported as an absent term rather than mapped onto something plausible that would return nothing.

A misspelling is read through rather than refused, and what it was read as is reported. The rule is the shape of the error, not its size: a trigger with letters dropped — "nonn" for "nonton", "bejar" for "belajar", "mah" for "murah" — is treated as the typing slip it is, while a word needing substitutions to reach a trigger is left alone, because two substitutions turn "cheap" into "chat" and "gaming" into "going" and neither is a misspelling of the other. Every correction is reported in the corrections field with the characters that went missing, so a reader can judge it instead of trusting it.

Use it before telkomsel_search_packages when the input is a customer's phrasing rather than a filter. Use telkomsel_search_packages directly when you already know the category, price range or quota you want.

Args:
  - phrase (string, required): what the customer said or typed, in Indonesian or English, e.g. "paket buat nonton film", "saya mau ke luar negeri", "paket buat main game".
  - msisdn (string, optional): number to count matches against, since the catalogue is personalised.
  - response_format (string, optional): "markdown" (default) or "json".

Returns (json): { phrase, tokensUsed, fillersDropped, intent, matchedOn, corrections, destination, absent, terms[{term, where, matched}], recommended, suggestedCall, intentCounts, note, otherIntents, provenance }.
Terms are ALTERNATIVES, not a conjunction: they must be searched one per call and merged. Joining them into a single query would AND them and return nothing — which is exactly the behaviour this tool exists to work around.
Returns an honest no-intent result, with per-token live counts, when nothing in the phrase maps to a catalogue concept.

phrase.description: What the customer said, in Indonesian or English, misspellings included, e.g. "paket buat nonton film", "saya mau ke luar negeri", "package for gaming".

msisdn.description: Telkomsel mobile number, local (081234455666) or international (6281234455666). Omit to use the session default set by telkomsel_set_default_msisdn.

response_format.description: "markdown" for a readable table, "json" for machine-readable output.

tools.name: telkomsel_get_config
tools.description:
Show the current session configuration for this Telkomsel MCP server.

Returns the effective default MSISDN (used by every tool when no explicit `msisdn` argument is given), where that value came from, the built-in fallback, and the valid Telkomsel number prefixes.

Call this first when you need to know which phone number the catalogue queries will be personalised for, or when a tool result looks like it belongs to an unexpected number.

Args:
  - none

Returns (JSON): { defaultMsisdn, defaultMsisdnInternational, source, builtInFallback, validPrefixes }

tools.name: telkomsel_set_default_msisdn
tools.description:
Change the phone number this session uses for every Telkomsel catalogue query.

This is the "swap the dummy number" switch. The new number takes effect immediately for all tools that omit an explicit `msisdn` argument, and stays set for the lifetime of the server process. Package availability, prices and recommendations are personalised per number, so changing it genuinely changes the catalogue you get back.

Validates the number first: it must normalise to a Telkomsel mobile prefix (0811, 0812, 0813, 0821, 0822, 0823, 0851, 0852, 0853, 0855) and be 10-13 digits.

Args:
  - msisdn (string, required): e.g. "081234455666", "6281234455666", "0812-3445-5666"

Returns (JSON): { previousMsisdn, defaultMsisdn, defaultMsisdnInternational }
Errors: an actionable message when the number is not a valid Telkomsel mobile number.

msisdn.description: New default number, local or international form.

tools.name: telkomsel_check_msisdn
tools.description:
Validate a phone number and ask Telkomsel what kind of customer it belongs to.

Normalises the input, checks the Telkomsel prefix and length, then queries the live API for the account type. Use this before a catalogue query to confirm the number is a real Telkomsel number and to learn whether it is prepaid (SIMPATI) or postpaid (Halo) — which determines whether prepaid package tools will return anything useful.

Args:
  - msisdn (string, optional): number to check. Omit to check the session default.

Returns (JSON): { input, normalized, international, valid, customerType?, product?, raw? }
Note: this only reads the public product type. It does not authenticate, and it cannot read balances, quota or personal data.

msisdn.description: Telkomsel mobile number. Accepts local (081234455666) or international (6281234455666) form. Omit to use the session default.

tools.name: telkomsel_get_default_number_hint
tools.description:
Explain in plain language which number the server is currently using and what that number can and cannot do.

Useful when a user asks "which number is this using?" or "how do I change the number?". This is a documentation tool: it makes no network calls.

Args:
  - none

Returns (string, markdown): current number, how to change it, and its limitations.

tools.name: telkomsel_list_products
tools.description:
List the top-level Telkomsel product catalogue — the 11 products shown under "Produk" on telkomsel.com.

Each entry carries the official display name, the positioning line the site uses ("Prabayar", "Modem WiFi", …), a stable slug for follow-up calls, a segment grouping, the machine-readable family, the official landing-page URL, a summary scraped from that page, and the page's own section headings.

Use this as the entry point when someone asks what Telkomsel sells, wants an overview of the product line, or needs the slug for telkomsel_get_product.

Args:
  - segment (string, optional): case-insensitive substring filter over the segment label, e.g. "Internet Rumah", "Kartu", "Internasional"
  - type (string, optional): exact product family, one of: mobile-prepaid, mobile-postpaid, mobile-prepaid-digital, home-fiber, home-broadband, home-wireless, home-wireless-device, converged, international, network-technology, device-bundling
  - response_format (string, optional): "markdown" (default) or "json"
  - fields (array, optional): which product fields to return. Omit for the recall-preserving default.

Returns: the matching products, plus a `selection` block naming the fields returned and a `provenance` block marking this as a snapshot. Bundled catalogue snapshot: 2026-10-16T06:46:11.893Z.
Note: this is the marketing catalogue. For purchasable packages with live prices, use telkomsel_search_packages.
Provenance: prose here is a snapshot, so it is authoritative for nothing that changes. Pass live=true to telkomsel_get_product for current page text.

segment.description: Substring filter over the segment label, e.g. "Internet Rumah".

response_format.description: "markdown" for a readable table, "json" for machine-readable output.

fields.description: Which fields to return. Omit for the recall-preserving default: every field except the multi-kilobyte HTML ones, each announced as a has* flag when you accept the default. A group name expands to that group's fields: content, identity, marketing, routing. Name a heavy field explicitly to include it, or pass ["all"] for absolutely every field.

tools.name: telkomsel_get_product
tools.description:
Get full detail for one Telkomsel product from the catalogue.

Returns the product's identity, the summary scraped from its official landing page, and the page's own section headings (which reveal what the product actually offers, e.g. "Paket Utama Halo", "Pilihan Modem Orbit", "Jangkauan 5G"). With `live: true` it re-reads the page from telkomsel.com right now instead of using the bundled snapshot.

Args:
  - id (string, required): product slug from telkomsel_list_products, e.g. "simpati", "halo", "byu", "indihome", "orbit", "eznet", "eznet-wireless", "telkomsel-one", "roaming", "5g", "bundling". A product display name such as "SIMPATI" also works.
  - live (boolean, optional, default false): re-scrape the official page instead of using the bundled snapshot
  - response_format (string, optional): "markdown" (default) or "json"
  - fields (array, optional): which product fields to return. Omit for the recall-preserving default.

Returns: the product record, plus `live` page data when requested.
Note: the JSON form adds a selection block naming the fields returned, and a provenance block saying whether the text came from the bundled snapshot or a live re-scrape.
Errors: lists the valid ids when the slug does not match.

live.description: Re-scrape the official page instead of using the bundled snapshot.

response_format.description: "markdown" for a readable table, "json" for machine-readable output.

fields.description: Which fields to return. Omit for the recall-preserving default: every field except the multi-kilobyte HTML ones, each announced as a has* flag when you accept the default. A group name expands to that group's fields: content, identity, marketing, routing. Name a heavy field explicitly to include it, or pass ["all"] for absolutely every field.

tools.name: telkomsel_list_segments
tools.description:
List the segment groupings and product families in the Telkomsel catalogue, with how many products fall into each.

Use this to pick a valid `segment` or `type` value for telkomsel_list_products without guessing.

Args:
  - none

Returns (JSON): { segments: [{ segment, count, products }], types: [{ type, count, products }], total }

tools.name: telkomsel_product_page_raw
tools.description:
Fetch one official telkomsel.com page and return only its headings and summary.

A narrow, live read of the public site. Use it to confirm the bundled catalogue is still accurate, or to look at a page that is not one of the 11 catalogued products (any telkomsel.com path).

Args:
  - path (string, required): site path beginning with "/", e.g. "/promo", "/5G", "/shops/home"
  - response_format (string, optional): "markdown" (default) or "json"

Returns: { url, httpStatus, pageTitle, summary, headings, fetchedAt }
Errors: an actionable message when the path is not on telkomsel.com or the fetch fails.

response_format.description: "markdown" for a readable table, "json" for machine-readable output.

tools.name: telkomsel_list_package_categories
tools.description:
List the live package categories available to a phone number.

These are the categories the Telkomsel purchase flow shows for that specific number (today: "Kamu Banget", "Internet", "Roaming", "Entertainment", "Telepon & SMS"). Availability and ordering are personalised, so two numbers can differ.

Use this before telkomsel_search_packages to pick a valid `category`, or to answer "what kinds of packages can I buy?".

Args:
  - msisdn (string, optional): number to personalise for. Omit for the session default.

Returns (JSON): { msisdn, totalPackages, categories: [{ categoryName, isRoaming, hasRecommendation, icon, subcategoryCount }] }

msisdn.description: Telkomsel mobile number, local (081234455666) or international (6281234455666). Omit to use the session default set by telkomsel_set_default_msisdn.

tools.name: telkomsel_list_subcategories
tools.description:
List the subcategory labels inside one package category for a phone number.

Subcategories are the bands the site groups packages into, e.g. "Super Seru Promo", "SIMPATI TikTok", "Hot Promo", "Netflix". Use one as the `subcategory` argument of telkomsel_search_packages to narrow a large category.

Args:
  - category (string, required): a category name from telkomsel_list_package_categories, e.g. "Internet". Case-insensitive; a partial name works.
  - msisdn (string, optional): number to personalise for. Omit for the session default.

Returns (JSON): { msisdn, category, subcategories: string[], withPackageCounts: [{ subcategory, packages }] }
Errors: lists the valid categories when the name does not match.

msisdn.description: Telkomsel mobile number, local (081234455666) or international (6281234455666). Omit to use the session default set by telkomsel_set_default_msisdn.

tools.name: telkomsel_search_packages
tools.description:
Search the live, personalised Telkomsel package catalogue for a phone number.

This is the main catalogue tool. It returns purchasable packages with real current prices, quota, validity and bonus items, personalised to the given number. Filter by category, subcategory, price range, quota range, masa aktif, roaming type, sort order, or a free-text query.

On quota, one thing decides whether a range filter is correct: `totalQuota` is not a data quota. Across the live catalogue it holds three different quantities — 60 forms in GB, 26 in voice minutes, 4 in SMS, and 30 packages empty. So a quota range requires `quota_unit`, defaults to GB, and excludes packages measured in another unit rather than comparing them. `filtersApplied.quotaRange` reports how many it excluded and why. The same field is behind `sort: smallest_quota | largest_quota`, which also only ranks packages measured in the requested unit.

When `category` Every search reads one complete catalogue and filters it here, category or not. The upstream listing returns at most twelve products per subcategory and offers no paging, so filtering through it returns a twelfth of a category and calls it the category: a flat fetch saw 315 of the 600 packages the same endpoint can be made to yield, and 24 roaming packages instead of 262. The catalogue is walked instead — price bands, then quota buckets, then rotated upstream orders, which is the only set of axes the endpoint honours. `filtersApplied.catalogueSize` is how many packages that walk collected; `filtersApplied.catalogueComplete` is false only if some subcategory group was still full at the cap after every axis was spent, and then `filtersApplied.cataloguePartial` names those groups, so a count is never quietly a floor.

A `query` decides membership; the filters decide it too; neither decides order. Results are ranked by Okapi BM25 over the same text the query was matched against, so the packages that actually carry a partner outrank the ones that merely mention it in a description — a search for "netflix" returns the four Netflix packages first rather than the twelve that contain the word. When nothing matches the query as written, it is retried with a small edit distance per term (the standard remedy for an exact index), and `filtersApplied.queryFuzzy` reports both that it happened and what the query was read as. A range spoken in words ("30GB sampai 50GB") is deliberately NOT answered: a text index cannot express BETWEEN, so it returns nothing and the caller should use min_quota/max_quota.

Args:
  - category (string, optional): package category, e.g. "Internet". Run telkomsel_list_package_categories for valid values.
  - subcategory (string, optional): narrow within a category, e.g. "Hot Promo". Requires category.
  - query (string, optional): free text, all words must match. Searched across package name, short and long description, category, subcategory, type, price, bonus names and descriptions. The long description carries the wording a customer would use, so "video", "tethering" and "youtube" reach packages that name neither. The price is indexed, so "75000" reaches offers at that price and "100rb" reaches those at 100000. The legal `terms` text is deliberately NOT searched: it is the same boilerplate on nearly every package, so matching it would return everything while meaning nothing.
  - sort (string, optional): lowest_price | highest_price | smallest_quota | largest_quota | longest_active_period
  - sort_by (object, optional): { metric, direction } — order by a computed metric instead of an upstream order. direction defaults to "desc". Built-in metrics: price_per_gb, price_per_day, saving, saving_percent, quota_per_1000, price_with_fee. Cannot be combined with sort.
  - compute (array, optional): metrics to compute per package, [{ name, expr }], up to 8. Each metric may read any published scalar field, the metrics declared before it, and the built-ins; the language is + - * / , comparisons, && and || (short-circuiting), a ? b : c, round/min/max/abs, numbers in either notation, and "text" or null literals.
  - quota (string, optional): coarse bucket — "0-5", "6-15", "16-25", "26-9999" (>25 GB), "-1" (unlimited). Prefer min_quota/max_quota for a precise range.
  - min_price / max_price (number, optional): rupiah bounds
  - quota_unit (string, optional): "GB" (default), "Min" or "SMS" — which allowance the quota range and quota sort measure
  - min_quota / max_quota (number, optional): allowance bounds, in quota_unit
  - min_validity_days / max_validity_days (number, optional): masa aktif bounds in days, from the parsed validity
  - roaming_type (string, optional): "Single Country" or "Multi Country" (Roaming category only)
  - region (string, optional): destination country from telkomsel_list_roaming_countries (Roaming category only)
  - recommended_only (boolean, optional): keep only packages the API marks as recommended for this number
  - limit (number, optional): 1-200, default 25
  - offset (number, optional): paging offset, default 0
  - refresh (boolean, optional): rebuild the catalogue cache instead of reusing it
  - msisdn (string, optional): number to personalise for
  - response_format (string, optional): "markdown" (default) or "json"
  - fields (array, optional): which package fields to return. Omit for the recall-preserving default.

**Computed metrics.** The upstream API sorts by five things and filters by price and quota; every other price question is arithmetic over fields it returns but cannot order by — which package is cheapest per gigabyte, which discount is the largest, what a gigabyte costs per day. That arithmetic happens here, over the whole match set, not in the caller.

  Built-in metrics, usable as `sort_by.metric` without declaring anything: `price_per_gb` = `quotaUnit == "GB" && quotaValue > 0 ? round(price / quotaValue) : null`; `price_per_day` = `validityDays > 0 ? round(price / validityDays) : null`; `saving` = `originalPrice > price ? originalPrice - price : null`; `saving_percent` = `originalPrice > price ? round((originalPrice - price) / originalPrice * 1000) / 10 : null`; `quota_per_1000` = `quotaUnit == "GB" && price > 0 ? round(quotaValue / price * 1000 * 100) / 100 : null`; `price_with_fee` = `price + fee`.

  A value that cannot be computed is **null, never 0**, and the response counts those rows and says why: `originalPrice` is 0 on 500 of 601 packages and means "no discount", so the naive `originalPrice - price` is a large negative number on almost every row and would sort the catalogue by a field that does not apply. Say `originalPrice > price ? originalPrice - price : null` — or sort by the `saving` metric, which is that expression. Rows a metric cannot be computed for sort last in both directions.

  Only the metrics named here are computed, plus the one in `sort_by`: a built-in used as a sort is computed without being declared, and a built-in that is neither named nor sorted by is not computed at all, so a caller who wants two of them asks for both.

  `computed.stats` covers every match, not the page: min, p25, median, mean, p75, max over the rows where the metric is a number, with the reason census for the rest. Computed values are attached to each returned package as `computed: { <name>: <value> }` even when `fields` did not select the fields they read.

Returns (markdown): a table of matches, a pagination footer and a provenance line. (json): { msisdn, matched, filtersApplied, page, packages, selection, computed, provenance }.
Note: the JSON default is recall-preserving — every package field except the multi-kilobyte `terms` and `longdesc` HTML, each announced as a has* boolean so its existence is visible without its cost. Ask for them by name, or pass ["all"]. A JSON listing is capped by its serialised size: the server renders the payload it is about to send and drops trailing records until that text fits, so a wide projection returns fewer records than a narrow one and the body is always parseable. `page.cappedForSize` says whether the cap applied. Page with the `page.nextOffset` the result reports, not offset + limit: under the cap a page returns fewer rows than `limit`, and advancing by `limit` skips rows silently.
Derived fields: `quotaValue`, `quotaUnit` and `validityDays` are computed by this server from the display strings, not returned by the upstream — telkomsel_get_capabilities lists them under derivedFields. Use them to compare; use totalQuota and totalValidity only to display.
Provenance: every result names the fields this route is authoritative for, so a live price is never confused with an indexed one.
Errors: names the valid categories when `category` does not match, and reports clearly when no package matches the filters.

subcategory.description: Subcategory within the category, e.g. "Hot Promo".

sort.description: Sort order applied by the Telkomsel API. Omit for the site default (lowest_price). Cannot be combined with sort_by.

sort_by.description: Order the matches by a computed metric. Cannot be combined with sort, which orders upstream.

metric.description: A built-in metric (price_per_gb, price_per_day, saving, saving_percent, quota_per_1000, price_with_fee) or the name of one declared in compute.

direction.description: asc for a cost per unit (price_per_gb, price_per_day), desc for an amount (saving, saving_percent). Rows the metric cannot be computed for sort last in both directions.

compute.description: Metrics to compute for every match. Read any published scalar package field, any metric declared earlier in this array, and the built-in metrics; use round/min/max/abs, comparisons, && , || and a ? b : c. A value that cannot be computed is null and the response says why row by row. Example: [{name: "saving", expr: "originalPrice > price ? originalPrice - price : null"}].

name.description: Name the result is reported under and that sort_by accepts, e.g. "saving".

expr.description: Arithmetic over package fields, e.g. "originalPrice > price ? originalPrice - price : null". Built-ins: price_per_gb, price_per_day, saving, saving_percent, quota_per_1000, price_with_fee.

quota.description: Quota bucket, as the API defines it. Coarse: prefer min_quota/max_quota for a precise range.

quota_unit.description: Which allowance quota filters and sorts measure. totalQuota holds data (GB), voice minutes or SMS, so a bare number is ambiguous.

min_quota.description: Minimum allowance, in quota_unit. Packages measured in a different unit are excluded, not compared.

region.description: Destination country, in either language and tolerating a misspelling: "Singapura", "Singapore" and "singapure" all resolve to the same packages. Both published spellings are always matched together, because they do not overlap — searching one alone reaches roughly half the roaming catalogue. A group name ("Asia Tenggara", "Eropa") works too.

recommended_only.description: Keep only packages marked recommended for this number.

offset.description: Number of matches to skip, for paging (default 0).

refresh.description: Rebuild the catalogue cache instead of using the cached copy.

msisdn.description: Telkomsel mobile number, local (081234455666) or international (6281234455666). Omit to use the session default set by telkomsel_set_default_msisdn.

response_format.description: "markdown" for a readable table, "json" for machine-readable output.

fields.description: Which fields to return. Omit for the recall-preserving default: every field except the multi-kilobyte HTML ones (longdesc, terms), each announced as a has* flag when you accept the default. A group name expands to that group's fields: billing, bonus, content, identity, internal, marketing, pricing, quota, routing, validity. Name a heavy field explicitly to include it, or pass ["all"] for absolutely every field. Narrow a sub-entity with a dotted name, e.g. "bonus.quota".

tools.name: telkomsel_get_package
tools.description:
Get the full detail of a package: price, quota, validity, every bonus item, description, and optionally the terms and conditions.

Identify the package with `ref` (durable, recommended), `id` (ephemeral: resolvable only while this process still remembers it, and only for the same number), or `name` (may match several variants — the same package name exists at different quota and price points).

IMPORTANT — ref vs id: the Telkomsel API mints a NEW `id` on every request, so an id is only usable for the rest of this server session. `ref` is derived from stable fields (`name@quota@price`) and can be reused in a later session, stored in a note, or handed to a user. Prefer `ref` whenever the value has to outlive the current turn.

Args:
  - ref (string, optional): durable reference from a search result, e.g. "super-seru-promo@53gb@100000".
  - id (string, optional): ephemeral id from a search result for the same number. It can stop resolving; prefer ref.
  - name (string, optional): package name, e.g. "Super Seru Promo". Case-insensitive partial match.
  - include_terms (boolean, optional, default false): include the full terms and conditions text.
  - refresh (boolean, optional, default false): rebuild the catalogue cache before falling back to a full scan.
  - msisdn (string, optional): number to personalise for.
  - response_format (string, optional): "markdown" (default) or "json"
  - fields (array, optional): which package fields to return. Omit for the recall-preserving default; pass ["all"] to include the terms and longdesc HTML.

Provide at least one of `ref`, `id` or `name`.
Returns: the full package record with its bonus breakdown and its `ref`. When a name matches several variants, the cheapest is shown in full and the alternatives are listed.
Note: offerId is the right key for a corpus index, because it does not change when only the price moves. ref is the right key for resolving this exact priced offer again.
Errors: suggests how to find the package when nothing matches.

ref.description: Durable reference from a search result, e.g. "super-seru-promo@53gb@100000".

id.description: Ephemeral package id from a search result in this session.

include_terms.description: Include the full terms and conditions.

refresh.description: Rebuild the catalogue cache before falling back to a full scan.

msisdn.description: Telkomsel mobile number, local (081234455666) or international (6281234455666). Omit to use the session default set by telkomsel_set_default_msisdn.

response_format.description: "markdown" for a readable table, "json" for machine-readable output.

fields.description: Which fields to return. Omit for the recall-preserving default: every field except the multi-kilobyte HTML ones (longdesc, terms), each announced as a has* flag when you accept the default. A group name expands to that group's fields: billing, bonus, content, identity, internal, marketing, pricing, quota, routing, validity. Name a heavy field explicitly to include it, or pass ["all"] for absolutely every field. Narrow a sub-entity with a dotted name, e.g. "bonus.quota".

tools.name: telkomsel_compare_packages
tools.description:
Compare two to ten packages side by side on price, quota, validity and what each one includes.

Fetches each package's current record and returns a comparison table plus computed facts: price per GB, the cheapest option, and the largest quota. Useful for "which of these is the best value?" questions.

Identify packages by their `ref` (durable, recommended — the ref column of telkomsel_search_packages) or by a same-session `id`.

Args:
  - package_refs (string[], required): 2-10 refs. A same-session package id also works. A short unique ref prefix, e.g. "super-seru-promo@53gb", is accepted too.
  - msisdn (string, optional): number to personalise for.
  - response_format (string, optional): "markdown" (default) or "json"

Returns (markdown): a comparison table plus a verdict line. (json): { packages, computed: { cheapest, largestQuota, bestValuePerGb } }
Errors: names the refs that were not found and points back at telkomsel_search_packages.

package_refs.description: Two to ten package refs (or same-session ids) to compare.

msisdn.description: Telkomsel mobile number, local (081234455666) or international (6281234455666). Omit to use the session default set by telkomsel_set_default_msisdn.

response_format.description: "markdown" for a readable table, "json" for machine-readable output.

tools.name: telkomsel_get_filter_options
tools.description:
Return the filter options the Telkomsel purchase flow itself offers: sort orders, the price range inputs, and the quota buckets.

Each option carries the exact `value` string the API expects, so you can pass them straight to telkomsel_search_packages without guessing. Also reports the live roaming-type options.

Args:
  - none

Returns (JSON): { filterSections: [{ sectionName, title, type, defaultValue, items }], roamingTypes: [{ name, value }], quotaBuckets }
Note: makes two read-only GET requests to the Telkomsel API.

tools.name: telkomsel_list_roaming_countries
tools.description:
List the destination countries Telkomsel roaming packages cover, in both Indonesian and English.

Use the returned name as the `region` argument of telkomsel_search_packages to find packages for one destination.

Args:
  - query (string, optional): filter by country name in Indonesian or English, e.g. "singapore" matches "Singapura".
  - limit / offset (number, optional): paging, default limit 40.

Returns (JSON): { total, matched, page, countries: [{ original, en }] }
Note: `original` is the Indonesian name, and it is the value the `region` filter of telkomsel_search_packages accepts. `en` is the English name, for matching an English question.

query.description: Country name in Indonesian or English.

offset.description: Number of matches to skip, for paging (default 0).

tools.name: telkomsel_get_offer_break
tools.description:
List the featured offer groups Telkomsel promotes, and optionally expand one into its packages.

The offer break is the promotional band the site shows (e.g. "Super Seru", "Seru Internet", "Bisa Bayar Nanti"), each with its own internal list of offer groups such as Promo, Combo, Weekly or RoaMAX.

Args:
  - offer (string, optional): name of an offer group to expand into its packages, e.g. "Seru Internet". Omit to just list the groups.
  - msisdn (string, optional): number to personalise for.
  - response_format (string, optional): "markdown" (default) or "json"
  - fields (array, optional): which package fields to return when expanding an offer.

Returns (JSON): { categories, limit, offers: [{ name, enabled, groups: [...] }] }, plus expansion as { expanded, packageCount, packages, selection, provenance, truncated }

offer.description: Offer group name to expand, e.g. "Seru Internet".

msisdn.description: Telkomsel mobile number, local (081234455666) or international (6281234455666). Omit to use the session default set by telkomsel_set_default_msisdn.

response_format.description: "markdown" for a readable table, "json" for machine-readable output.

fields.description: Which fields to return. Omit for the recall-preserving default: every field except the multi-kilobyte HTML ones (longdesc, terms), each announced as a has* flag when you accept the default. A group name expands to that group's fields: billing, bonus, content, identity, internal, marketing, pricing, quota, routing, validity. Name a heavy field explicitly to include it, or pass ["all"] for absolutely every field. Narrow a sub-entity with a dotted name, e.g. "bonus.quota".

tools.name: telkomsel_list_credit_options
tools.description:
List the pulsa (airtime top-up) denominations offered for a phone number, with the active-period extension each one grants.

Use this when a user asks how much pulsa they can buy or how much extra active period a top-up gives.

Args:
  - msisdn (string, optional): number to personalise for.
  - response_format (string, optional): "markdown" (default) or "json"

Returns (markdown): a table of denominations. (json): { msisdn, total, options }

msisdn.description: Telkomsel mobile number, local (081234455666) or international (6281234455666). Omit to use the session default set by telkomsel_set_default_msisdn.

response_format.description: "markdown" for a readable table, "json" for machine-readable output.

tools.name: telkomsel_get_faq
tools.description:
Fetch the official FAQ entries for a Telkomsel product line.

Args:
  - product (string, optional): "simpati" (default) or "halo".
  - msisdn (string, optional): number to personalise for.
  - response_format (string, optional): "markdown" (default) or "json"

Returns: the FAQ content as published on the site. The upstream shape varies, so markdown output is best-effort and json is returned whenever the structure is not a simple question/answer list.

msisdn.description: Telkomsel mobile number, local (081234455666) or international (6281234455666). Omit to use the session default set by telkomsel_set_default_msisdn.

response_format.description: "markdown" for a readable table, "json" for machine-readable output.

tools.name: telkomsel_aggregate_packages
tools.description:
Summarise a set of packages instead of listing them.

telkomsel_search_packages answers "which packages match". This answers "what do they cost, and what do I tell a customer about the range" — the questions a single listing cannot, because the answer is a statistic over hundreds of rows and a listing shows twenty-five.

It takes exactly the same filters as telkomsel_search_packages and runs the same pipeline, so an aggregate can never describe a different set of packages than a search for the same filters. Where telkomsel_compare_packages summarises 2-10 packages the caller already named, this summarises everything that matches.

Args:
  - category, subcategory, query, quota, quota_unit, min_quota, max_quota, min_validity_days, max_validity_days, min_price, max_price, roaming_type, region, recommended_only: identical to telkomsel_search_packages.
  - refresh (boolean, optional): rebuild the catalogue cache instead of reusing it.
  - top (number, optional): how many entries in each shortlist, default 5, max 20.
  - msisdn (string, optional): number to personalise for.
  - response_format (string, optional): "markdown" (default) or "json".

Returns (json): { msisdn, matched, filtersApplied, price{min,max,median,mean}, pricePerGb{min,median,considered,excludedNotGb}, quota{byUnit,byBucket}, validityDays{min,max,median,unmeasured}, byCategory, cheapest[], bestValuePerGb[], notes[], provenance }.
Money is integer rupiah. Price per GB is computed only over packages whose allowance is actually measured in GB, and the count it skipped is reported rather than hidden.

region.description: Destination country, in either language and tolerating a misspelling. See telkomsel_search_packages.

msisdn.description: Telkomsel mobile number, local (081234455666) or international (6281234455666). Omit to use the session default set by telkomsel_set_default_msisdn.

response_format.description: "markdown" for a readable table, "json" for machine-readable output.

instructions:
Read-only access to the Telkomsel product catalogue.

Start with telkomsel_get_capabilities when you need to decide whether this route fits a question, which tool to call,
or which fields to ask for. It is static and costs no upstream request.

Two layers are available:
1. Product catalogue (telkomsel_list_products, telkomsel_get_product): the 11 top-level products on telkomsel.com.
2. Package catalogue (telkomsel_search_packages and friends): live, purchasable packages with real prices, personalised per phone number.

Every package query is personalised by MSISDN. The session default is 081234455666; change it with telkomsel_set_default_msisdn or pass msisdn per call.
Listing tools accept a "fields" argument for caller-driven field projection; omit it for the recall-preserving default.
Nothing here purchases, activates, or modifies an account.

If you are indexing this catalogue rather than answering from it, read the resource telkomsel://catalog first.
It lists every document worth embedding with a content hash for incremental sync, and states what must never be
embedded because it changes per number. Tools are for live answers; resources are for the stable corpus.
